Prevention: Prevent the use of broad spectrum insecticides, as these will kill the pests natural enemies such as ladybird beetles and predatory mites.
Citrus rust mites are only a cause for concern when found in high populations.
To keep population levels low maintain suitable conditions for predatory species such as other insects and birds.
Prune to maintain good air circulation within the trees.
Control weed populations within the orchard by uprooting.
Monitoring: To observe for mite infestations, use a hand lens to examine green fruit in tree canopies.
Note that citrus mites are usually found in the stylar end of fruit.
If one or more fruit are found to be infested, undertake direct control measures.
Citrus mites are commonly found in mixed populations with broad mites ( Polyphagotarsonemus latus ).
Citrus rust mites are 0.1-0.2 mm long, with yellow-brown bodies.
Discolouration of fruit, turning grey-brown due to mite feeding.
Undeveloped fruit that do not store well.
Leaves and twigs bronze from heavy infestations.
If more than 30% of trees are infested then consider direct action measures.
Direct Control: If available in your country, release predatory mites such as
Agistemus exsertus (release roughly 2 00 mites/tree, seek advice from local extension officers).
Use of white oil spray (3 tablespoons of cooking oil with 4 litres of water and half a tablespoon of detergent soap).
Spray the underside of leaves and re-spray after 3 to 4 weeks if neccesary.
Use of soap solution spray (2 tablespoons of soap/ washing liquid with 4 litres of water).
Spray the underside of leaves and re-spray after 3-4 weeks if necessary.
